hits.title: What is Kubernetes CrashLoopBackOff? And how to fix it | Sysdig
hits.snippet: Basically, it’s an exponential delay between restarts (10s, 20s, 40s, …) which is capped at five minutes. When a Pod state is displaying CrashLoopBackOff, it means that it’s currently waiting the indicated time before restarting the pod again.

hits.title: How to Troubleshoot a Kubernetes Pod Stuck in CrashLoopBackOff
hits.snippet: Kubernetes sees the pod terminate and restarts it, assuming it should be running continuously as a daemon. This creates a CrashLoopBackOff loop despite no actual "errors" occurring. Fix: Ensure the main process in your container runs in the foreground and blocks execution indefinitely (like a web server or a tail -f command for debugging).
